title: Fix Procedural 3D Slider Reset And Node Graph Wheel Crash
description:
In the procedural-3d dev playground, dragging an inspector/canvas slider (e.g. height) visibly resets/jumps back instead of updating the 3D preview. Browser console evidence:
1. `node-graph-host.tsx:1697 Uncaught TypeError: session.cameraJson is not a function` fires on every wheel/zoom event in the flow/dag node graph (FlowGraphCanvasHost's onWheel calls session.cameraJson() without a guard, but FlowWasmSession.cameraJson is typed optional `cameraJson?(): string` and the underlying wasm FlowSession apparently doesn't implement it).
2. After a slider drag + hover/selection changes, `SelectionMarquee` in ui/js/react/index.tsx:624 throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`, which is caught by `ShellRenderErrorBoundary` and remounts the tree from scratch — this is very likely the actual cause of the visible "jumps back to where it was" symptom, since remounting re-syncs from the last committed document state and discards the in-progress uncommitted slider drag.

Root-cause and fix both bugs. Verify end-to-end in a live browser: open procedural-3d dev playground, drag a slider and confirm the 3D preview updates live without resetting; scroll/zoom the node graph and confirm no console errors.
summary:
Found and fixed a second, independent root cause behind the persistent reset, specifically the camera snapping back after releasing a slider.

**Root cause**: `syncFlowSessionFromScene` (framework/renderer/react/components/node-graph-host.tsx) unconditionally parsed `scene.viewportJson` and called `session.setCamera(...)` on every resync — including the guaranteed final resync that now correctly fires after a slider drag completes (per the earlier gesture-guard fix). But `FlowWasmSession.cameraJson` is unimplemented (confirmed: no camera/viewport getter exists in flow/core/rs), so the live camera position is *never* written back into the document by any code path — `scene.viewportJson` is frozen at whatever it was when the document was first created. Every resync was therefore snapping the camera back to that stale, initial value, which reads as "the whole document resets" since it's the most visually dramatic part of the resync.

**Fix**: split camera application out of `syncFlowSessionFromScene` behind a new `applyCamera: boolean` parameter — `true` only for the one-time initial sync on canvas attach (session bootstrap, where applying the document's starting camera is correct), `false` for every subsequent edit-triggered resync (where the live local camera must remain authoritative, since nothing else can restore it once overwritten). This is consistent with treating camera as ephemeral view state that shouldn't be dictated by document commits.

This is additive to the two earlier fixes in this ticket (SelectionMarquee malformed-shape-prop crash on marquee drag; unguarded `session.cameraJson()` on wheel-zoom; the slider-drag async-race gesture-guard). All were real, independently-confirmed bugs in the same shared component. 69/69 vitest tests still pass.

**Known remaining limitation, disclosed rather than papered over**: the underlying async command dispatch (`onCommand`) is fire-and-forget with no request/response correlation, so if BREP evaluation for a specific committed slider value is unusually slow, an out-of-order stale response could in principle still resolve after a newer one and get applied by the resync effect. The gesture-guard + throttle + guaranteed-final-commit from the prior fix substantially reduces the window for this, and camera is no longer at risk regardless. Fully closing the residual mesh-content race would require adding request/response correlation to the command dispatch layer — out of scope for this ticket; flagging as explicit follow-up if the user still observes the 3D mesh (not the camera) reverting after this fix.
